newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity closes down, but up from lows.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity closes down, but up from lows.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures closed lower, but rebounded from intra-day lows amid some short-covering, traders said Thursday.
"We had a significant down movement early on, but people bought back toward the end of the day," said one dealer.
Traders said further weakness in second- and third-quarter over-the-counter prices, particularly at Palo Verde, put downward pressure on the futures complex.
"Summer prices are starting to look a little toppy," said another trader.
She noted that weaker summer natural gas prices and expectations of plentiful hydropower supplies through at least July led to the shift in sentiment.
April California Oregon Border (COB) settled down 16 cents at $9.22 per megawatt hour (MWh) after hitting a new contract low of $8.85 per MWh.
May COB closed 15 cents lower at $9.25 and June was down 14 cents at $10.31.
The Palo Verde April contract was unchanged at $12.90 after trading as low as $12.75 per MWh, while May was down 10 cents at $13.65 per MWh and June ended 30 cents lower at $15.00.
PV deferreds were also lower, with July closing down 35 cents at $19.60 per MWh.
NYMEX said an estimated a total of 286 COB and 376 PV contracts traded on Thursday.
In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were expected to average near to slightly below normal through early next week, with showers and upper elevation snows likely for Saturday through Tuesday.

In the Southwest, temperatures were expected to be below normal through Sunday, then were called to rebound to slightly above normal Monday and Tuesday. Precipitation will average above normal through Sunday, with showers and mountain snows likely.
